dissents.topic: Lazy LoRA registration via mutable flag

positions.position: Caching is_registered on the TritonLoraConfig avoids reloading weights on every request and is a meaningful perf win for a feature that is otherwise unusable at scale.

is_registered is mutated outside any lock from an async handler; concurrent first-requests for the same LoRA will both read False, both load the weights, and the TRT-LLM backend may see duplicate or racing registrations. A check-and-set under a lock (or sending weights every time and letting the backend dedupe by task_id) is safer.

dissents.topic: Returning None vs raising on malformed multi_lora.json

positions.position: Preserving the existing 'return None on Exception' behavior keeps startup resilient when a model is misconfigured.

Swallowing all exceptions (including the new ServerError path's siblings) and only printing a traceback hides real misconfiguration. Operators starting a server with a broken multi_lora.json silently get a model with no LoRAs, which is worse than a clear error.

issues.description: Race condition on lora_config.is_registered under concurrent requests
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, the code checks `if not lora_config.is_registered` and then sets it to True after attaching weights. This is shared mutable state on a TritonLoraConfig instance reused across all requests, mutated from async request handlers with no lock. Two simultaneous first-time requests for the same LoRA will both observe is_registered=False, both load and send the full weights, and a third concurrent request arriving after one sets True but before TRT-LLM has actually registered the task may send only task_id and fail. At minimum this should be guarded by an asyncio.Lock per lora_config, or weights should always be sent and dedup handled by task_id semantics in the backend.

issues.description: np.load called synchronously inside async request path on every cold LoRA
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request now performs blocking disk I/O (np.load of model.lora_weights.npy and model.lora_config.npy) inside what is invoked from an async FastAPI handler. LoRA weight tensors can be tens to hundreds of MB; loading them on the event loop thread will stall all other in-flight requests for the duration. Weights should be preloaded at model-metadata-parse time (memoized on TritonLoraConfig) or loaded via asyncio.to_thread / a background executor.

issues.description: _get_lora_config return type annotation lies; returns None but signature says TritonLoraConfig
issues.detail: `def _get_lora_config(self, model_name: str, lora_name: Optional[str]) -> TritonLoraConfig:` returns None when lora_name is None or model has no lora_configs. Type should be `Optional[TritonLoraConfig]`. More importantly, when `model_metadata` is None (model_name not found in the dict), the code does `model_metadata.lora_configs` and will raise AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError. Either guard against missing metadata or rely on the upstream validation to ensure the model exists before this is reached — but the current code is unsafe.

issues.description: Backend selection logic for _parse_lora_configs is inverted/confusing
issues.detail: The call site passes `backend if self.backend is None else self.backend`. This means when `self.backend` (frontend-level override) is set, it always wins, ignoring the per-model `backend` discovered from Triton. That is likely the opposite of what's intended for a mixed repository: a single TRT-LLM-forced server arg would force vLLM-style parsing on TRT-LLM models or vice versa. Worth a comment at minimum, and likely should be `self.backend or backend` only when self.backend is meant as a fallback.

issues.description: Variable shadowing of lora_config_path inside parse loop
issues.detail: `lora_config_path` is bound at line ~659 to `version_path/multi_lora.json`, then rebound inside the inner loop to `lora_path/model.lora_config.npy`. On the next iteration of the outer per-repo loop, the rebinding is irrelevant, but inside the for-each-lora loop the reuse of the same name for two semantically different paths is a readability and bug-magnet hazard. Rename the inner one to `lora_config_npy_path`.

issues.description: task_id assignment is global counter across repos but reset across process restarts; potential collision with backend's own task IDs
issues.detail: `lora_task_id = 1` and incremented per LoRA discovered. TRT-LLM treats lora_task_id as a cache key; if any other client or another model also sends task_id=1..N for a different LoRA, the cached weights are wrong. There is no namespacing per model. Consider hashing (model_name, lora_name) into the task_id space, or documenting the assumption that this frontend owns the task_id namespace.

issues.description: Broad `except Exception` swallows real errors and only prints a traceback
issues.detail: In _parse_lora_configs the outer try/except catches ServerError and re-raises (good), but the bare `except Exception` returns None after printing the traceback. This will silently disable LoRAs on any unexpected error (permissions, encoding issue, schema drift). At minimum log at error level via the project's logger instead of print, and consider re-raising for non-FileNotFoundError cases since a malformed multi_lora.json is operator misconfiguration, not a recoverable condition.

Inside the per-lora loop in _parse_lora_configs there is `print(f"backend: {backend}")` for every LoRA entry. This is debug output that will spam stdout on every server startup proportional to LoRA count. Remove it.

issues.description: traceback.print_exc added to FastAPI exception handlers duplicates logging
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, and embeddings.py each grow `import traceback` and `print(traceback.format_exc())` in the ServerError and generic Exception handlers. FastAPI/uvicorn already log unhandled exceptions; printing to stdout duplicates and is not structured. Use the project's logger if extra context is needed, or remove these debug prints before merge.

issues.description: Return type annotation on _parse_lora_configs is wrong
issues.detail: Signature says `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but the function now returns `List[TritonLoraConfig]` (or None). The annotation is stale from the rename and misleads readers and type checkers.

issues.description: Test no longer guarded by backend availability and may run with neither installed
issues.detail: `_backend = "vllm" if is_vllm_installed() else "tensorrtllm"` falls through to tensorrtllm even when TRT-LLM isn't installed; the previous `@unittest.skipUnless(is_vllm_installed(), ...)` decorators were removed. If neither backend is present, tests will attempt to run and fail in confusing ways. Add a symmetric `is_trtllm_installed()` check and skip the class if neither is available.

issues.description: test_parse_lora_configs ignores the tensorrtllm-mode result and may mask regressions
issues.detail: The renamed test calls `parse_lora_configs(... , "tensorrtllm")` without inspecting the return, and the function will return None on any I/O error in the test fixtures since the mock_llm/test_models fixtures don't include npy files. The only check left is the `expect_error`/ValueError path. Add explicit assertions that the parsed configs match expected names/paths/task_ids for the trtllm branch.

issues.description: Sed-based config.pbtxt patch in qa/L0_openai/test.sh is a fragile WAR
issues.detail: `sed -i 's/dims: \[ -1, 3 \]/dims: \[ -1, 4 \]/'` is exactly the kind of pin that breaks the day TRT-LLM updates the template. The FIXME at least flags it, but ideally generate the config with the correct dims directly via the fill_template script's parameters or pin the upstream TRT-LLM version that requires this patch.

issues.description: Doc example uses repo-relative paths that don't exist outside the test setup
issues.detail: The README example shows `inflight_batcher_llm/tensorrt_llm_bls/1/luotuo-lora-7b-0.1-weights` as the path in multi_lora.json. In practice the path is resolved relative to the process CWD, not the model repo. The doc should either show absolute paths or call out the path-resolution semantics explicitly to avoid users filing confused issues.
`is_registered: Optional[bool] = False` — Optional implies None is valid, but the code only ever uses it as a bool. Type should be plain `bool = False`.

issues.description: Reusing _validate_*_request error and _get_lora_config error duplicates the 'Unknown LoRA' check
issues.detail: Both _validate_chat_request / _validate_completion_request and _get_lora_config raise 'Unknown LoRA: …' independently. Once validation passes, _get_lora_config's `raise ClientError` should be unreachable. That's fine defensively, but consider routing through one path so the messages can't diverge ('for model: {request.model}' vs 'for model: {model_name}').

Generic `tensorrtllm_models` is already there; adding `tensorrtllm_mistral_models/` suggests one ad-hoc local artifact rather than a stable pattern. Consider `tensorrtllm*_models/` or document why this specific dir is special.

review.summary: The PR extends multi-LoRA support to the TensorRT-LLM backend in the OpenAI frontend, refactoring the prior vLLM-only LoRA name parsing into a more general TritonLoraConfig dataclass that carries task_id, path, and a registration flag. The feature direction is correct and the README/test coverage additions are welcome, but there are two correctness concerns that should block merge: (1) `is_registered` is shared mutable state mutated from async request handlers without synchronization, and (2) `np.load` of potentially-large LoRA weights happens inline in the async request path on first use, blocking the event loop. Beyond that, several debug `print` statements and `traceback.print_exc` calls were added to hot paths, the type annotations on the refactored function and helper are stale, the backend-selection ternary at the call site looks inverted, and the tests no longer skip cleanly when neither backend is installed. The brittle `sed` patch in test.sh and a globally-monotonic task_id with no per-model namespacing are also worth addressing before this lands.
